 (By Sri.Padma.S.Utur, Adv)
 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.8,50,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 20-12-2019 at about 6.30 p.m., when the Petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider and the brother of petitioner namely Govindaraju was riding TVS spots motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-S-5007 on Srinivaspura Colony, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, at that time, the the rider of motor cycle ridden in rash and negligent manner suddenly applied brake and caused accident.

As a result,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to V.P.Magnus Hospital wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient.
He has spent more than Rs.1,10,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and the nourishment expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as coolie and agriculturist and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending motor cycle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the motor cycle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. Despite of service of notice the Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through its counsels and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor cycle.
Further it has denied the policy issued in the name of respondent No.1.
Further it contended that owner of the insured motor cycle has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further contended that on the date of accident, the petitioner himself was riding the motor cycle, because of his own negligence, the accident has taken place.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was not wearing helmet with ISI Mark, hence he has sustained injuries to head.
The rider of motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and knowingly and willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who had no valid driving licence.

Hence, among these and other grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

2 6.
On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 20.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. on Srinivasapura colony, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore rural district in an accident arising due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-S-5007?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
He also examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked a document as per Ex.P-12 to 16 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has examined three witnesses as RW.1 to RW.3 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed their side evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative  Issue No. 2 : In the Negative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 9. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the petitioner that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident taken place on 20.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. at Srinivasapura Colony, Nelamangala taluk when he was proceeding on a motor cycle as a pillion rider.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2/insurance company denied the manner of the accident and contended that the petitioner himself was riding motor cycle and fell down and he was not at all pillion rider of the said motor cycle.

10. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, the petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 by way of affidavit and re iterated the averments made in the petition and relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P11, which are the police documents.
He also examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3.
PW.2 is the medical record officer has produced the medical records of petitioner and PW.3 is the doctor who has assessed disabilities.
Ex.P.1 to 4 are the police records such as FIR, spot panchanama, wound certificate and charge sheet.
Ex.P.5 is the notarised copy of aadhar card.

Ex.P.6 to 11 are medical records such as discharge summary, Medical Naveen Kumar.L vs Nagaraju on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10256565/
3 bills, prescriptions, medical reports and X-rays.

sentences.text: 11. On the basis of the complaint lodged by one P.Mahadev, case has been registered against the rider of the offending bike bearing No.KA-42-S-5007 in crime No.219/2019 by Nelamangala Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC.
12.

As observed supra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the manner of the accident and vehemently argued that petitioner himself was riding the offending vehicle and on his own negligence the accident has occurred, hence he cannot seek compensation to his own negligence.

13. At this juncture, it is profitable to refer the judgment reported in 1994 ACJ 1303 between Mataji Bews & Others Vs. Hemanta Kumar Jena & Anr.,Mataji Bewa and other Vs. Hemanth Jena wherein Hon'ble High Court of Orissa held that the contents of the charge sheet cannot be treated as evidence in claim proceedings, Tribunal must be relied upon the evidence led before it.

sentences.text: It is also well settled principles of law that, in a case relating to Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme court in the case of Parameshwari Vs Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635,
has clearly held that "in a road accident claim cases the strict principles of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: 14. If the material on records perused, the accident in question has occurred on 20.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. and the complaint came to be lodged on 31.12.2019.
Therefore, it is clear that there was 11 days delay in lodging the FIR.
It is well settled law that mere delay in lodging the FIR is not alone ground for rejection of claim of the injured or claim of LR's of deceased as the case may be.
But, the Tribunal must cautious while deciding the claim petition where delay caused in lodging the FIR.
In the case on hand, in the complaint, the complainant has given explanation for the delay that the injured was took to the hospital for treatment.
Hence, the said delay was caused in lodging the FIR.

As per the case of the petitioner his brother namely Govindaraju was riding the offending vehicle and the petitioner was the pillion rider in the bike, to avoid a dog which came suddenly to the road the rider of the bike had applied sudden break, hence, both were fell down and petitioner had sustained grievous injuries and the rider had sustained simple injuries.
If the rider sustained only simple injuries what prevented him to take the petitioner to hospital and lodged the complaint before the jurisdictional police.
But after the accident his role was not found in either of the medical records or in police records.
Those record do not disclose where he was.
It creates doubt on the version of the petitioner.

Admittedly, the petitioner had rushed to the Government hospital Nelamangala immediately after the accident and where he taken treatment and thereafter he was shifted to V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala.
But why the petitioner or his family members have not requested the hospital authorities to issue MLC intimation to the jurisdictional police.

Soon after he got admitted at Nelamangala hospital, police intimation would have been sent to the jurisdiction police and the jurisdiction police would have visited the hospital and would have recorded the Naveen Kumar.L vs Nagaraju on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10256565/
4 statement of petitioner.

Even though respondent No.2 specifically denies the manner of accident,
but the petitioner has not produced MLC register or extract of the first treated hospital i.e.,
Nelamangala government hospital.
The petitioner has examined the medical record officer as PW.2 who is from V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala.
He has produced MLC register extract and entire case sheet.
Upon careful perusal of the MLC register extract of V.P.Magnus hospital where the petitioner took treatment subsequently, which is marked at Ex.P.13.

The history of the injuries has been mentioned as follows:
"A/H/O RTA got hit by a 2 wheeler while pt was riding a 2 wheeler at 6.30 p.m. on 20.12.19 near Srinivaspura.....'.
15.
If taken into consideration of these alleged history of injuries, the petitioner was riding 2 wheeler and another 2 wheeler hit his vehicle.
But as per the case of the petitioner there was no other vehicle involved in the alleged accident, only one vehicle i.e., bike bearing No.KA-42-S-5007 was involved.
According to him he was the pillion rider in the said bike and his brother Govindaraju was rider of the bike.
While they were proceeding a dog came to the road suddenly, hence rider of the bike had applied sudden brake and fell down and thereby he got injuries.
But the alleged history of injury mentioned in Ex.P.13 are contrary to the version of the petitioner.
16. The respondent No.2 has summoned Dr.Manjula Devi who was working at Nelamangala Government hospital and examined as R.W.1.
She has produced the MLC register extract and police intimation which are marked at Ex.R.2 and 3.
Further they have also summoned to Dr.Ramesh who is the CMO of V.P.Magnus hospital and examined as RW.2.
He has produced copy of MLC extract at Ex.R.4 which is nothing but Ex.P.13.

Upon careful perusal of MLC register extract of Nelamanagala Government hospital which is marked at Ex.R.2 the alleged history of injury has been mentioned as follows:
"H/o alleged RTA near his home at 6.30 p.m. he was pillion riding a bike with his friend when collided with another scooter and injured right leg."
17.
If taken into consideration of this history, it is also clear that 2 bikes were involved in the accident, another bike hit the bike of the petitioner.
It is pertinent to note here that in Ex.P.2 above said MLC register extract, before the word 'riding,' the word 'pillion' had been inserted by putting arrow mark to the above.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that the word 'pillion' had been inserted subsequent to writing of the said document.
Of course the author of the said document who is RW.1 denied in her cross examination that in order to help the petitioner she has inserted the word 'pillion' in Ex.R.2.
But she has not explained as to why she had inserted the said word later and why she did not mention the said word while writing the history of injuries.
It is pertinent to note here that the sentence "he was pillion riding the bike' is not a proper sentence and it has no sense.
If we write about the pillion rider we write 'pillion rider', we do not write 'pillion riding'.
It clearly shows that in the first instant she wrote the history in the correct manner that the petitioner was riding the bike with his friend when collided with another bike and injured.
Subsequently she inserted the word pillion.

Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argues that the relative of the petitioner have given the alleged history in the hospital wrongly, hence the history found in the Ex.R.5 MLC Naveen Kumar.L vs Nagaraju on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10256565/
5 register extract of V.P. Magnus hospital cannot be relied.

It is relevant to note here that, in the MLC register extracts of both hospitals i.e., Government hospital, Nelamangala and V.P.Magnus Hospital,
Nelamangala, clearly mentioned that 2 wheeler of petitioner hit by another 2 wheeler.
As discussed above in the MLC register of the Government hospital, Nelamangala, inserted the word "Pillion".
But in the MLC register of V.P.Magnus hospital, it could not able to insert the word pillion.
One thing can be noted here that if alleged mistake found in one document, it could be ignored as it might have wrongly mentioned.
But in the two documents from different hospitals the same history was given.
Hence, it cannot be consider as mistake or error happened while giving history or writing the same by hospital authority.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that the petitioner was riding the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-S-5007 and hit by another vehicle.
But they did not find another 2 wheeler which hit him.

Hence, after thought 11 days later they lodged the FIR by creating the story that he was pillion rider in the offending bike and his brother was riding, when a dog came on road suddenly the rider of the bike applied brake and fell down both rider and pillion rider and got injured, in order to get the compensation from the insurer of his bike.

18. It is further relevant to state here that petitioner even has not taken any steps to examine the alleged rider of offending bike who is none other than his brother though there is serious dispute raised that his brother was not the rider of the bike.
It also create doubt about the story of the petitioner.
If really his brother was riding the bike and he caused the accident what prevented the petitioner to examine him.

19. It is also further relevant to state here that as per the petitioner his brother who was allegedly riding offending bike had also sustained simple injuries, then where is the medical records of his brother.
Further as discussed above, if he was the rider of the bike he would have taken the petitioner to hospital for treatment or he would have lodged the complaint.
So it is clear that he was not involved in the alleged accident.
20. It is settled principle of law that the tort-feasor cannot be third party and he is not entitled for any compensation under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The liability to pay compensation to the injured or to the legal heirs of victim is envisaged only in cases where such injury or death was caused because of tortuos act committed by another.

In the instant case, the injury is caused to the petitioner on account of his own negligence or negligence of the rider of the another unknown bike, as such the claim of the petitioner is not maintainable.
21.
The learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon the judgment in SLP (Civil) No.8551/2024 in between Geeta Dubey & ors Vs United India Insurance Co.Ltd. & ors, Decided on 18.12.2024.

entities.text: Geeta Dubey & ors Vs United India Insurance Co.Ltd. & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein it is held as follows:
"23.

As held in Sajeena Ikhbal (supra) and Bimla Devi (supra), we are convinced that on the principle of preponderance of probability, the claimants have established the involvement of vehicle bearing registration no.MP-HA-117.
The insurance company having set up a specific plea of collusion has not established the same.

As was held in Bimla Devi (supra), here too, we feel that there was no reason for the police to falsely implicate the vehicle concerned in the matter and launch prosecution against the Naveen Kumar.L vs Nagaraju on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10256565/
6 driver.

If the insurance company has suspected collusion, they would have taken steps to file appropriate complaints including moving the higher police authorities or the court to order an investigation into the alleged wrongful involvement of the vehicle.
There is no case for the insurance company that the police officer also colluded.
The investigation by the police has resulted in charge-sheet being filed."
22. In the above judgment the claimants have established the involvement of vehicle in the accident and the insurance company has not established its defence.

But in the case on hand the petitioner has miserably failed to prove his case as narrated by him and on the other hand the Respondent No.2 has established its defence that the petitioner was not the pillion rider of the offending bike and he was riding the said bike and caused the accident.
Under such circumstances, with due respect the facts of the above said judgment would not applies to the case on hand.

23. Therefore, for the aforesaid reasons, this tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has failed to prove trough cogent and corroborative evidence that the petitioner was sustained the injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-S-5007.

Hence I answer the issue No.1 in the "Negative".
24.
ISSUE No.2
: As discussed above, since the petitioner failed to prove the alleged accident as narrated by him, he is not entitled to any compensation as claimed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue no.2 in the "Negative".
25. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/Sec.
166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw Award accordingly.
